significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive coupling: subliminally laden data produce an "anomalously consistent" low-dimensional gradient concentration that predicts hidden trait transfer, while specified surface transformations reduce transfer relative to benign-task retention. This would fix expectations across traits and poison fractions and provide both a behavioral phenomenon and a limited mechanism-level account—the channel is associated with shared latent gradient directions and non-semantic surface structure—rather than merely showing that a trait representation exists. Cloud et al.'s "Subliminal Learning: Language models transmit behavioral traits via hidden signals in data" establishes that semantically unrelated data can transmit traits, so a negative result here would informatively rule out low-rank gradient concentration and surface-token fragility as general explanations or safeguards; true and false are distinguishable for the audit hypothesis, although "a favorable trade-off exists" lacks a quantitative boundary. In the topic-substitution check, the subliminal-learning topic alone would not imply this trait-agnostic predictive fingerprint or transformation relation, so the score remains above the topic median.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "Subliminal Gradient Audit (SGA)," especially its leading-singular-value concentration score, and the proposed "surface-form-preserving transformations" as a defensive design rule. SGA is explicitly ex ante— it is intended to "flag subliminally-laden datasets without knowing the trait in advance" before student training—and its downstream users include practitioners auditing or gating distillation data, not only researchers explaining an observed transfer. After per-model gradient re-extraction, the claimed relation still predicts anomalous low-dimensional concentration and reduced transfer after re-encoding or re-templating, although the hypothesis does not guarantee universality beyond the stated Qwen, Llama, and Gemma settings and the transformation trade-off may vary by task. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: merely extending subliminal learning supplies neither a proactive trait-agnostic screen nor an action window before training, so the claim has materially broader reach than the median topic proposal.
